sources.citation: Sande, Hannah. 2017. Distributing morphologically conditioned phonology: Three case studies from Guébie. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley. 207 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Ch. 2.2 'Guébie phonology' (segments, syllable structure V/CV/CLV, minimality, tone, vowel harmony; pp. 10-29) never mentions stress or accent; 'stress' occurs only in bibliography entries. Tone: four-height system with level and contour melodies (p. 22).

sources.note: 40-page overview of the whole phonology (tone, harmony, reduplication, syllable alternations, implosives); the most likely place for an explicit remark on the absence or presence of word stress. CC BY-NC hybrid OA, but Wiley's an automated-access block blocks our network; a browser or a Harvard login download would open it.
